evidence: Cato Agr. 2.4: quae reliqua opera sient
terms.comment: Latin puts the adjective with its noun: agmen reliquum, the rest of the column. Lewis & Short: reliquus is what remains of a thing; cēterī the others besides those named. “As for the rest”: quod reliquum est (Cic. Att. 16.15.3, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: the rest of (a time, a quantity)
evidence: Liv. 39.13: ubi reliquum vītae dēgere tūtō posset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The rest of the day, of one’s life: reliquum diēī, reliquum vītae.
In letters and talk: cētera cōram, the rest when we meet. As an accusative of respect, “in other respects”: cētera laetus (Hor. Ep. 1.10.50).

phrases.latin: prīmā deinde lūce castra mōta et agmen reliquum incēdere coepit
phrases.english: then at first light the camp was struck and the rest of the column began to move

phrases.latin: ubi cognita aequō animō sient quae reliqua opera sient, cūrārī utī perficiantur
phrases.english: when he has calmly found out what work is left, let him see that it gets finished

phrases.latin: cētera cōram agēmus. haec properantēs scrīpsimus.
phrases.english: we’ll deal with the rest face to face. I have written this in a hurry.
the rest is fine; one thing surprises me
the rest of the way would be level or downhill

phrases.latin: tōta quidem pōnātur anas, sed pectore tantum et cervīce sapit: cētera redde cocō
phrases.english: serve the duck whole, by all means; but only the breast and neck have any taste: give the rest back to the cook
